new_statements.quote: Boa-Yewu is a tone language with two underlying tones, High (H) and Low (L). A tone is associated with a tone-bearing unit. A High and a Low tone can be combined on one tone bearing unit. Tone in Boa-Yewu has a distinctive function, both in the lexicon and in the grammar. The number of tonal minimal pairs in the lexicon is limited. Tone plays a higher functional load in the grammar [...] LowHigh and HighLow tones are probably composite contours, a sequence of two level tones. [Motingea 2005: 30:] Il existe deux tons simples bas (`) et haut (´) ainsi que deux complexes montant (ˇ) et descendant (ˆ). [...] Les tons ont une double valeur: lexicale et grammaticale.
new_statements.translation: Motingea 2005: 'There are two simple tones, low and high, as well as two complex ones, rising and falling. ... The tones have a double value: lexical and grammatical.'
new_statements.citation: de Wit, Gerrit. 2020. Boa-Yewu, a Bantu language with a seven-vowel system and ATR vowel harmony. In G.J. van der Wal et al. (eds.), Essays on African languages and linguistics in honour of Maarten Mous (ASCL Occasional Publication 41), 417-447. Leiden: ASCL.
new_statements.locator: sec. 2.3 'Tonemes', pp. 421-422 (PDF pp. 434-435 of the volume); corroborated by Motingea 2005, sec. 2.1.4 'Tons', p. 30
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Files checked in (1) de Wit 2020 (lines 17550-17600 = printed pp. 421-422): sec. 2.3 'Tonemes' opens exactly 'Boa-Yewu is a tone language with two underlying tones, High (H) and Low (L). A tone is associated with a tone-bearing unit. A High and a Low tone can be combined on one tone bearing unit. Tone in Boa-Yewu has a distinctive function, both in the lexicon and in the grammar. The number of tonal minimal pairs in the lexicon is limited. Tone plays a higher functional load in the grammar...' and later 'LowHigh and HighLow tones are probably composite contours, a sequence of two level tones.' -- verbatim as quoted (the [...] elides footnote refs and examples). Sec. 2.4 syllable structure V…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Boa (both the Yewu dialect of Bambesa and the leɓóale of Buta) is described as a two-tone (H/L) Bantu language with lexical and grammatical tone and surface contour tones from two tones on one TBU; neither modern description, nor the older colonial materials, says anything about word stress or accent placement.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in any source examined.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress. (Motingea notes vowel length arising from coalescence/contact, i.e. a mora distinction, and H-tone 'proéminence' in HL/LH contraction, which is tonal neutralisation, not stress.)
new_statements.domain_note: Tone statements concern the word (lexical roots, CVCV nouns) and verbal inflection; no phrase-level prominence or intonation discussed. de Wit describes the Yewu dialect (Bambesa territory; Guthrie C402), Motingea 2005 the leɓóale of Buta (C44) and the lebaate (Benza/Bati) variety.
new_statements.identity_note: de Wit 2020 describes Boa-Yewu, the Bambesa-territory dialect (Ethnologue 'Bwa' [bww]; Maho C402), which Glottolog subsumes under bwaa1238; Motingea 2005 describes leɓóale/libóali of Buta (C44, the other main Boa dialect) and, in ch. 3, lebaate (Benza/Bati, also filed under bwaa1238 by Glottolog via Koloma 1993 'baati'). Motingea & Kadite 2022 concerns letakpú, a near-extinct secret register of the Bokpendú Boa, not the everyday language. Halkin 1910 / de Calonne 1909 'Ababua, libwâlè/libati' = the same two dialect groups. Not to be confused with Lebéo/Ngelima (Gérard 1924; C45, ngel1238) or Pagibete (C401, pagi1244).

sources.locator: sec. 2.3 'Tonemes', pp. 421-422 (PDF pp. 434-435 of the volume); corroborated by Motingea 2005, sec. 2.1.4 'Tons', p. 30
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent. Sec. 2.3 'Tonemes' (pp. 421-423): 'Boa-Yewu is a tone language with two underlying tones, High (H) and Low (L)'; tone distinctive in lexicon and grammar; HL/LH contours = two tones on one TBU; 2.4 syllable structure V, CV, CGV, N. The word 'accent' occurs only in the orthographic note (acute accent marks H tone).

sources.citation: Motingea Mangulu, André & Dieudonné Tazanaba Kadite. 2022. Notes préliminaires sur le letakpú: une langue ɓóa spécifique quasi éteinte sur les rives de la Bomokandi (Bas-Uélé, RDC). Afrikanistik-Aegyptologie-Online 2022, 1-47. doi:10.18716/ojs/aaeo/2022_3484
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Sec. 2.4 Tonologie (par. 11): notation too unreliable to treat tone; provisionally two registers (bas, haut), no complex tone observed; melodic H in past narrative as in most 'Bóa bloc' languages. Describes a near-extinct secret/warrior register of the Bokpendú Boa, not the main language; cites Motingea 2019b ms. 'Notes sur le système tonologique du ɓóa-yéwú'.

sources.citation: Motingea Mangulu, André. 2005. Leboale et lebaate: langues bantoues du plateau des Uélé, Afrique Centrale (ILCAA Language Monograph Series 3). Tokyo: ILCAA. xvi+199 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent (scanned of pp. 5-35, 119-133 and bibliography grepped; tone/syllable pages read as images). Leboale sec. 2.1.4 Tons (pp. 30-35): 'Il existe deux tons simples bas et haut ainsi que deux complexes montant et descendant'; tones have lexical and grammatical value; rules: contraste tonal, harmonie tonale, neutralisation, abaissement. 2.1.5 Syllabes (p. 35): open syllables V, (N)CV, (N)CSV, N; vowel section (p. 12) notes long vowels from contact/coalescence = mora distinction. Lebaate sec. 3.1.3 Tons (p. 130): same two-tone system.
